title: The Book of Daniel Timeline
sub: The Fiery Furnace, the Lions' Den · One Like a Son of Man
desc: Exiled Judean nobility rise to prominence in the Babylonian and Persian courts through uncompromising faithfulness, moving from court tales of miraculous deliverance into apocalyptic visions of successive empires and a coming everlasting kingdom.

eras.label: Era One · Daniel 1
eras.name: Daniel Resolves Not to Defile Himself
eras.dates: Exiled Judean nobility are trained for Babylonian royal service, and one young man's quiet resolve over diet becomes the book's opening test of loyalty

events.title: Daniel Resolves Not to Defile Himself With the Royal Food
events.detail: Taken captive to Babylon and enrolled in royal training, Daniel and his three friends request a simple vegetable diet rather than the king's rich food and wine, emerging healthier than their peers and gifted with extraordinary wisdom and insight.

verses.text: “Daniel made up his mind that he would not defile himself with the royal delicacies or the royal wine.”

eras.label: Era Two · Daniel 2
eras.name: Nebuchadnezzar's Dream — the Statue of Four Kingdoms
eras.dates: A forgotten dream and an impossible royal demand become the occasion for Daniel's first great interpretive triumph

events.title: The King Demands the Dream Itself, Not Just Its Meaning
events.detail: Nebuchadnezzar demands his wise men reveal both a forgotten dream and its interpretation on pain of death; when even Babylon's finest fail, Daniel and his friends pray, and the mystery is revealed to Daniel in a night vision.

verses.text: “Let the name of the true God be blessed from eternity even to eternity, for wisdom and power belong to him.”

events.title: A Statue of Gold, Silver, Bronze, Iron, and Clay: a Kingdom That Will Never Be Destroyed
events.detail: Daniel reveals and interprets the dream of a great statue representing successive world empires, struck down by a stone that becomes a mountain filling the whole earth: the everlasting kingdom God himself will establish.

verses.text: “In the days of those kings the God of heaven will raise up an everlasting kingdom that will not be destroyed and a kingdom that will not be left to another people.”

eras.label: Era Three · Daniel 3
eras.name: The Fiery Furnace — Even If He Does Not Rescue Us
eras.dates: Refusal to bow to a golden statue leads Daniel's three friends into a furnace, and out again unscathed, accompanied by a fourth figure

events.title: Our God Is Able to Rescue Us: But Even If He Does Not
events.detail: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue, are thrown into a furnace heated seven times hotter than normal, and emerge completely unharmed alongside a mysterious fourth figure, astonishing the king into praising their God.

verses.text: “If our God whom we are serving exists, he is able to rescue us… But if he does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not pay homage to the golden statue.”

eras.label: Era Four · Daniel 4
eras.name: Nebuchadnezzar's Madness — the Most High Rules Over Human Kingdoms
eras.dates: A second dream, warning of coming humiliation, comes true when Nebuchadnezzar's own pride goes unchecked. (This chapter's opening three verses belong to the Aramaic text's previous chapter; references here follow the Aramaic numbering, marked inline in the NET text as “(3:31)” and “(4:1)”.)

events.title: A Tree Cut Down: Break Away From Your Sins by Doing What Is Right
events.detail: Nebuchadnezzar dreams of a great tree chopped down to a stump, and Daniel interprets it as a warning that the king himself will be driven from human society until he acknowledges that the Most High rules over human kingdoms, urging him toward repentance while there's still time.

verses.text: “Nebuchadnezzar the king, to all peoples, nations, and language groups… Peace and prosperity!” (Numbered 4:1 in most English translations.)

events.title: My Sanity Returned to Me: I Praise and Exalt the King of Heaven
events.detail: Twelve months later, at the height of his pride, Nebuchadnezzar is struck exactly as warned, living like an animal for seven periods until his sanity returns and he publicly praises the King of heaven whose authority is everlasting.

verses.text: “I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, for all his deeds are right and his ways are just.”

eras.label: Era Five · Daniel 5
eras.name: The Writing on the Wall — Weighed and Found Wanting
eras.dates: A drunken banquet using sacred temple vessels is interrupted by a disembodied hand, and the empire falls the very same night

events.title: Mene, Mene, Teqel, Pharsin: Belshazzar Weighed and Found Wanting
events.detail: King Belshazzar drinks from Jerusalem's sacred temple vessels at a great banquet, and a hand appears writing on the wall; Daniel interprets the message as the end of the kingdom, and Belshazzar is killed that very night as Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians.

verses.text: “You have not glorified the God who has in his control your very breath and all your ways!”

eras.label: Era Six · Daniel 6
eras.name: The Lions' Den — Three Times Daily He Was Praying
eras.dates: Jealous rivals engineer a religious trap under a new king, and Daniel's uncompromising prayer life costs him a night among lions, and vindicates him completely. (The Aramaic text's chapter division falls one verse earlier than most English translations here, marked inline in the NET text as “(6:1)”; every following verse in this chapter runs one number higher than in most English Bibles.)

events.title: Three Times Daily He Was Kneeling and Praying: the Lions Could Not Harm Him
events.detail: Jealous officials trick King Darius into an unchangeable edict banning prayer to any god but the king, knowing Daniel will keep praying toward Jerusalem regardless; thrown into a den of lions, Daniel emerges completely unharmed, and his accusers are thrown in instead.

verses.text: “My God sent his angel and closed the lions' mouths so that they have not harmed me because I was found to be innocent before him.” (Numbered 6:22 in most English translations.)

events.title: Darius Decrees That All People Revere the God of Daniel
events.detail: Astonished by Daniel's deliverance, Darius issues an empire-wide decree that all people revere the living God of Daniel, whose kingdom will never be destroyed.

verses.text: “I have issued an edict that throughout all the dominion of my kingdom people are to revere and fear the God of Daniel.” (Numbered 6:26 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Seven · Daniel 7
eras.name: Four Beasts — One Like a Son of Man
eras.dates: The book's tone shifts from court tales to apocalyptic vision, opening a second half built around Daniel's own dreams of world empires and a climactic heavenly courtroom

events.title: Four Beasts From the Sea: One Like a Son of Man Given Everlasting Dominion
events.detail: Daniel dreams of four terrifying beasts representing successive kingdoms, culminating in a heavenly courtroom where the Ancient of Days takes his seat and one like a son of man is given an everlasting dominion that will never be destroyed: a title Jesus later applies directly to himself.

verses.text: “With the clouds of the sky, one like a son of man was approaching… To him was given ruling authority, honor, and sovereignty… his kingdom will not be destroyed.”

eras.label: Era Eight · Daniel 8
eras.name: The Ram and the Goat — Until 2,300 Evenings and Mornings
eras.dates: A second vision, now in Daniel's native Hebrew rather than Aramaic, narrows the focus to a specific coming conflict between two named empires

events.title: A Ram Struck Down by a Goat: Gabriel Explains the Vision
events.detail: A two-horned ram representing Media and Persia is overrun by a fierce goat representing Greece, whose large horn breaks into four; the angel Gabriel explains the vision points toward the desecration and eventual restoration of the sanctuary.

verses.text: “The ram that you saw with the two horns stands for the kings of Media and Persia. The male goat is the king of Greece.”

eras.label: Era Nine · Daniel 9
eras.name: Daniel's Prayer of Confession — Seventy Weeks Determined
eras.dates: Studying Jeremiah's prophecy of a 70-year exile, Daniel prays one of the Old Testament's most thorough confessions and receives one of its most debated prophecies in return

events.title: We Have Sinned: O Lord, Hear! O Lord, Forgive!
events.detail: Reading Jeremiah's prophecy that the exile would last 70 years, Daniel prays an extended, humble confession on behalf of his whole nation, appealing not to their own righteousness but entirely to God's abundant compassion.

verses.text: “To the Lord [Adonai] our God [Elohim] belong compassion and forgiveness, though we have rebelled against him.”
“Lord [Adonai], hear! Lord [Adonai], forgive! Lord [Adonai], pay attention, and act! Don't delay, for your own sake, O my God [Elohim]!”

events.title: Seventy Weeks Have Been Determined for Your People
events.detail: Gabriel arrives mid-prayer with one of the most intensely studied and debated prophecies in Scripture: seventy 'weeks' of years determined concerning Jerusalem, an anointed one cut off, and a coming covenant-breaker who brings sacrifices to a halt.

verses.text: “From the issuing of the command to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed one, a prince arrives, there will be a period of seven weeks and sixty-two weeks.”

eras.label: Era Ten · Daniel 10
eras.name: A Glorious Man — the Prince of Persia Withstood Me
eras.dates: Daniel's final vision opens with an overwhelming angelic encounter and an unusual glimpse behind the scenes of spiritual warfare over nations

events.title: The Prince of Persia Opposed Me for 21 Days: Michael Came to Help
events.detail: After three weeks of mourning, Daniel encounters an overwhelming angelic figure who reveals that a spiritual 'prince of Persia' delayed his arrival for three weeks until the archangel Michael intervened: a rare glimpse of unseen conflict behind earthly political events.

verses.text: “The prince of the kingdom of Persia was opposing me for 21 days. But Michael, one of the leading princes, came to help me.”

eras.label: Era Eleven · Daniel 11
eras.name: Kings of the North and South — a Detailed Prophecy of Coming Wars
eras.dates: The book's longest and most historically detailed chapter traces centuries of conflict between rival dynasties with startling precision

events.title: Kings of the North and South: the Abomination That Causes Desolation
events.detail: In remarkably specific detail, the angel traces generations of conflict between the 'king of the north' and 'king of the south,' including a coming figure who will profane the sanctuary, halt the daily sacrifice, and set up 'the abomination that causes desolation.'

verses.text: “His forces will rise up and profane the fortified sanctuary, stopping the daily sacrifice. In its place they will set up the abomination that causes desolation.”

eras.label: Era Twelve · Daniel 12
eras.name: Many Will Awake — Those Who Are Wise Will Shine Like the Stars
eras.dates: The book closes with one of the Old Testament's clearest statements of bodily resurrection, sealing its visions until an appointed time of the end

events.title: Many Who Sleep in the Dust Will Awake: the Wise Will Shine Like the Stars
events.detail: Michael the great prince arises during an unprecedented time of distress, and the book delivers one of the Old Testament's clearest statements of bodily resurrection (some awaking to everlasting life, others to shame) before sealing the visions until the appointed time of the end.

verses.text: “Many of those who sleep in the dusty ground will awake—some to everlasting life, and others to shame… those who have insight will shine like the brightness of the heavenly expanse.”
